original_query: SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(SUM(t5.f2 * t6.f1), 0) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE COALESCE(SUM(CAST(t5.EXPR0 * t6.f1 AS INTEGER)), 0) END FROM (SELECT JOB, COALESCE(SUM(SAL), 0) AS EXPR0, COUNT(*) AS f2 FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A' GROUP BY JOB) AS t5 INNER JOIN (SELECT NAME, COUNT(*) AS f1 FROM DEPT GROUP BY NAME) AS t6 ON t5.JOB = t6.NAME
rewritten_query: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE COALESCE(SUM(CAST(s.expr0 * s.f1 AS INTEGER)), 0) END FROM (SELECT ej.job, ej.expr0, COUNT(*) AS f1 FROM (SELECT JOB, COALESCE(SUM(SAL), 0) AS EXPR0 FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A' GROUP BY JOB) AS ej INNER JOIN DEPT AS d ON ej.job = d.name GROUP BY ej.job, ej.expr0) AS s

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The null-check condition COALESCE(SUM(t5.f2 * t6.f1), 0) = 0 is redundant complexity: since t5.f2 and t6.f1 are both COUNT(*) values (always >= 1 for each group), the sum is zero only when the join produces no rows. It can be replaced by a simple COUNT(*) = 0 existence check.

The DEPT subquery groups the entire 450k-row table by NAME even though only names matching the filtered EMP jobs are needed. Push the join with the filtered EMP job groups into the DEPT aggregation (join DEPT to the filtered EMP subquery before grouping) so counts are computed only for matching names.

Join the filtered/aggregated EMP results directly to the raw DEPT table and aggregate per job, instead of pre-aggregating all of DEPT then joining. With an index on DEPT(NAME), this becomes an efficient nested-loop index lookup for the few matching jobs.

Remove the now-unused f2 (COUNT(*) per EMP job group) since it was only needed for the redundant null-check. Add supporting indexes: CREATE INDEX ON emp (ename, job) INCLUDE (sal); and CREATE INDEX ON dept (name);. The CAST(... AS INTEGER) must stay inside SUM to preserve per-row truncation semantics.
